content.text:
Finding submitted.

**Summary:** ASSIGN is a **deviation** (walk-away territory) in this agreement:

- **Article XXIV(c) (p0149)** flatly prohibits any Licensee assignment or transfer of licence rights without Licensor's consent, with no affiliate or M&A carve-out, and imposes no reciprocal restriction on Licensor — failing even the fallback (no mutual successor-assignment right).
- **Article XX(a) (p0134)** goes further: our Change of Control *automatically terminates* the Agreement and all our licences unless Licensor consents, with Licensor deemed reasonable in refusing on competitive or self-interest grounds.

**Redline (preferred level, three surgical replaces):**
1. Adds a consent-free carve-out for assignment to an Affiliate or an M&A successor, keeping the rest of the sentence and the "void" mechanic verbatim.
2. Replaces the dangling "Section 13.4(a)" change-of-control cross-reference with a Licensor-side restriction: no assignment without our consent (not unreasonably withheld) and never to our competitor.
3. Converts Article XX(a) into an express statement that a Change of Control neither terminates the Agreement nor gives Licensor a termination right, while preserving the "CHANGE OF CONTROL" definition lead-in and Article XX(b).

Noted but not flagged here: Article XXII's right of first refusal on a sale/merger (ROFR/MFN rule) and the separate licence-transfer restrictions in Articles II and VI (IP rule).
